- A short sampling plan that explains how you select sessions for audit (time ranges, tenant selection, seed criteria).

Sophie —

Appreciate the clear scope. We can support this window. High-level plan below; I attached a compact playbook and a proposed owner roster so your team can route follow-ups.

Quick answers up front:
- Sampling approach: stratified by tenant tier (enterprise / enterprise-sandbox / self-serve), then by peak- and off-peak windows; within each tenant we seed by recent customer session IDs and by randomly-sampled start timestamps to ensure coverage across model variants and lengths.
- Telemetry fields included: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_variant, routing_node, routing_policy, kv_cache_hit(boolean), token_index, token_timestamp, prompt_length, response_length, and a minimal stacktrace where relevant. PII is redacted; tenant identifiers are hashed.
- Mapping: we’ll produce a one-page control cross-reference that ties each telemetry field to CAIQ assertions for Traceability, Observability, and Runtime Isolation.

Owners (proposed):
- Telemetry extract & redaction: Irene Choi (Applied ML / Instrumentation)
- Control crosswalk & narrative: Marissa Cole (Security Programs)
- Legal & transfer gating: Kimberly Park (Privacy & Compliance)

Deliverables and timing:
- Sampling-playbook-v1 (attached) — today (this thread)
- Owner roster + gating checklist (attached) — today
- Initial redacted telemetry extract (representative / ~48 sessions) — delivery by 2028-02-18 if approved
- Full secure transfer (SFTP/secure folder + audit ACLs) — by 2028-02-20

If that timeline works, please reply with the prioritized control IDs (or ask us to choose the top-10 for Aurora). We can scope down the extract to a 24-session quick-check if you prefer a faster verification.

Jordan Blake

Looping in detailed notes for the extraction so Sophie knows what to expect. Quoted below is the outbound extract template we’ll use (redaction rules included).

On Thu, Feb 16, 2028 at 10:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sophie —
>
> Appreciate the clear scope. We can support this window. High-level plan below; I attached a compact playbook and a proposed owner roster so your team can route follow-ups.

Extraction template (will be zipped):
- manifest.csv (list of session_ids included, hashed tenant id, timestamp window, model_variant)
- events.log (newline JSON lines: request_id, epoch_ms, event_type, payload_keys*)
- tokens.tsv (tab-separated: request_id, token_index, token_text_redacted, token_timestamp_ms)

Redaction rules:
- user_input: keep structural markers only (length, token hashes); strip raw text unless explicitly permitted by legal.
- tenant_id: SHA256 truncated to 10 chars + tenant_tier label.
- IPs / hostnames: omitted.
- stack traces: include module path but redact line numbers.

Operational notes:
- We will not include un-sampled PII.
- KV cache hits are boolean in events.log; we will provide a short explanation tying cache_hit semantics to control requirement RT-CAIQ-07.
- Routing decisions will include policy name (e.g. "latency-fallback", "cost-priority") but not node internal IDs.

I’ll produce the first 48-session extract by Friday morning and post the secure link (Drive with strict ACL + audit logs). Marissa will draft the control crosswalk narrative.

- Irene

Attachment: runtime-telemetry-extract-README.md (referenced in zip)
